pages_note: The sub-pages of the Guide, in the order the navigation lists them. Each draws the views it names: continue, path, connections, features, tips. The first is where the section opens. Every lesson has its own address, /guide/lesson/<id>.

pages.name: Your path
pages.title: Your path
pages.lede: Eight stages, from saying hello to Rouh running work for you. Each lesson is one thing to do, and ends with the next.

pages.name: Enabling Rouh
pages.title: Enabling Rouh
pages.lede: Each connection unlocks a part of Rouh, and Rouh ticks its lesson when it sees it connected. Start with Google and your phone.
pages.icon: <rect x="3" y="8" width="18" height="8" rx="4"/><circle cx="16" cy="12" r="2.4"/>

pages.name: Pro tips
pages.title: Pro tips
pages.lede: For when you already use Rouh: small habits that make it much faster.

hero.title: Your path to everything Rouh can do
hero.fresh: Start with the first lesson. Each takes a minute or two, and Rouh ticks most of them by itself when it sees you do them.
hero.done: You have done every lesson on the path. Pro tips has the small habits that make Rouh faster.

talk_note.text: Say it in the message box at the bottom of the chat, typed or with the microphone. The answer appears in the chat; pages and tables appear on the canvas.

stages.title: Meet Rouh
stages.why: Ten minutes: what Rouh is, how to talk to it, and where things show up.

lessons.title: What Rouh is
lessons.outcome: After this you know the parts of Rouh and what each does for you.

cover.alt: A diagram: Rouh in the middle, joined to its eight parts: your screen, your workspace, background work, memory, time, decisions, trusted people and safety.

summary: Rouh is one assistant you talk to the way you would talk to a person. The same Rouh reads your mail, keeps your calendar, runs work in the background and remembers what you teach it.
Round it are the parts it works with. You do not need to learn them first: each lesson on your path shows one when you need it.

parts.name: Your screen
parts.text: The chat is where you and Rouh talk. The canvas beside it is where Rouh puts pages, tables and pictures. The orb, the small circle in the bottom-left corner, is a live picture of what Rouh is doing.

parts.name: Your workspace
parts.text: Everything you work on is a task with steps inside it, and every task has a number, like 58, with steps 58-01, 58-02.

parts.name: Background work
parts.text: When something takes real work, Rouh hands it to an assistant that works in the background while you carry on. Metabolism lists every piece of it.

parts.name: Memory
parts.text: Rules say how Rouh must always or never act, Vocabulary holds your own words, Thoughts keeps your ideas, and Boxes hold secrets the AI never sees.

parts.name: Time
parts.text: Clockwork holds everything Rouh will say or do at a time, once or on repeat. Goals are things you want to reach, with a plan Rouh writes.

parts.name: Decisions
parts.text: Whenever Rouh needs your answer, the question lands in one list, Decisions, with the answer Rouh recommends.

parts.name: Trusted people
parts.text: The people Rouh may answer and act for when they write to it, each with what they may ask.

parts.name: Safety
parts.text: Anything that sends, shares, publishes, pays or deletes stops and asks you first. Text from outside, such as an email, is read as information and never obeyed. The Security stage shows all of it.

lessons.title: Talk to Rouh
lessons.outcome: After this you know where to type to Rouh, and where its answers appear.

cover.alt: The chat: your message on the right, Rouh's answer on the left, and the message box at the bottom.

summary: Everything starts with a sentence. You type it in the message box at the bottom of the chat, or say it out loud. This is the one place you talk to Rouh: every lesson after this one says what to say, and you say it here.

how.text: Find the message box: the wide box at the bottom of the chat that says Type to Rouh. Press it and type what you want, in plain words.

image.alt: The chat with its four parts numbered: the message box, Send, your words and Rouh's answer.

how: Press Enter, or the blue arrow at its right end, to send. Shift and Enter starts a new line instead.
Rouh's answer appears in the chat, under your words. Pages, tables and pictures appear on the canvas beside the chat (the next lessons show it).

how.text: If you cannot see the chat, it has been put away to a narrow bar at the left of the screen. Press that bar, Show the chat, and it comes back.

image.alt: The chat put away: a narrow bar at the left edge of the screen, numbered, which brings it back.

how: On a phone the chat and the canvas take turns: the button at the top right switches between them.
says: Hello Rouh, what can you do for me?
Call this chat Holiday plans.
What did I ask you yesterday?
Explain that more simply.

lessons.title: Talk by voice
lessons.outcome: After this you can talk to Rouh with your hands free, and hear it answer.

cover.alt: The Voice panel open above the message box, with Turn on the microphone, Voice replies and Dictate.

summary: You can speak to Rouh instead of typing. The voice controls are under one button at the left end of the message box. Nothing listens until you turn the microphone on.

how.text: Press the Voice button: the small person with sound waves, first on the left under the message box. A panel opens above it.

image.alt: The Voice button and its panel, numbered: the button, the microphone, voice replies and dictate.

how: Press Turn on the microphone. Allow the microphone if the browser asks. Speak, and Rouh answers when you pause.
Voice replies decides whether Rouh reads its answers out loud. Leave it on to listen, or turn it off to read.
For a long message, press Dictate (or Ctrl, Shift and Space), say all of it, then press Dictate again. A pause never ends your turn.
Press the microphone again to turn it off. Off means off: nothing is heard until you turn it on again.
says: Hi Rouh, can you hear me?
Read me my next three calendar events.
Stop talking.
Talk more slowly.

lessons.title: Use the canvas
lessons.outcome: After this you know where pages, tables and pictures appear, and how to change them.

cover.alt: The screen at a desk: the chat on the left and the canvas on the right, holding a page.

summary: The canvas is the wide panel beside the chat, where Rouh puts what is easier to see than to read: a page, a table, a plan or a picture. Every card on it has its own address, so you can open it again later or send it to someone.

how.text: Ask for something to look at, such as a page or a table. It opens on the canvas, to the right of the chat.

image.alt: The chat and the canvas side by side, numbered, with the button that puts the canvas away.

how: Ask for changes in plain words, such as Make it shorter. Rouh redraws the card, and keeps every version.
The panel button in the canvas's top right corner, Hide the canvas, puts it away to a narrow bar on the right; press that bar to bring it back. The cross beside it closes the page that is open.
On a phone the canvas is behind the chat: press the button at the top right to switch to it and back.
To keep a card with your work, ask Rouh to file it into a task.
says: Make a page with a three-day plan for Lisbon.
Show that as a table.
Make it shorter.
File that card as a step of the Lisbon task.

lessons.title: Read the orb
lessons.outcome: After this you can see at a glance what Rouh is doing, and open the menu.

cover.alt: The bottom-left corner of the screen, with the orb: a small round circle with rings round it.

summary: The orb is the small circle in the bottom-left corner of the screen. It sits over the menu when the menu is open, and over the page beside it when the menu is closed. It is a live picture of everything Rouh is doing, and it is also the button that opens the menu.

how.text: Find the orb: the small round circle in the bottom-left corner. The rings round it are how busy the machine is.

image.alt: The bottom-left corner of the screen, numbered: the orb, and the message box beside it.

how.text: Press the orb once: the menu opens from the left, with every part of Rouh. The orb turns into a cross; press it again to close the menu.

image.alt: The menu open, numbered: the cross that closes it, the dark bar that opens the orb, and the groups of the menu.

marks.label: Open the orb over the whole screen

how: To open the orb over the whole screen, press and hold the circle, or open the menu and press the dark bar beside the cross.

how.text: Over the whole screen, each branch is a piece of work going on, and a branch marked Needs you is waiting on you: press it to see why. With nothing running, it is a single calm light.

image.alt: The orb open over the whole screen, with nothing running: one light in the middle, and its controls at the top right.

marks.label: Put the orb back in its corner

how: Press the cross at the top right, or Escape, to put it back in its corner.
says: What are you working on right now?
Is anything waiting on me?

lessons.title: Stop a turn
lessons.outcome: After this you can stop Rouh in the middle of an answer.

cover.alt: The chat, with the message box at the bottom and its blue Send button at the right end.

summary: Sometimes you have heard enough. You can stop Rouh mid-answer without losing anything it already started in the background.

how.text: While Rouh is answering, the blue Send button at the right end of the message box turns into Stop.

image.alt: The right end of the message box, numbered: Send, which becomes Stop while Rouh answers.

marks.label: Send, and Stop while Rouh answers

how: Press Stop, or press Escape. The answer ends where it was.
Work Rouh already started in the background carries on. To stop that too, say so.
says: Tell me a long story about the sea.
Stop that run.

stages.title: Connect your life
stages.why: The four connections that unlock the most. Each lesson says exactly where to click.

lessons.title: Connect Google: Gmail, Calendar and Drive
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh can read and answer your mail, keep your calendar and find your files.

cover.alt: The Email and calendar page under Connections, with the Google app's settings and Connect Google.

summary: The one connection that unlocks the most: once it is on, your inbox, your calendar, your Drive and your Docs are all in one conversation.
how: Open the menu (press the orb), then Anatomy, then Connections, then Email and calendar.
The first time on this Rouh, an administrator sets up its Google app on the same page: copy the redirect address into Google Cloud, fill in Client id and Client secret, and press Save.
Press Connect Google, pick your account and allow what Google asks for.
Back in Rouh, the page names the connected account, and this lesson ticks itself.
says: What came into my inbox this morning?
What is on my calendar tomorrow?
Find the slides I made last week.
Help me connect my Gmail, one step at a time.

connection.needs: Your Google account. The first time, whoever runs this Rouh gives it a Google app: a client id and secret from Google Cloud.

lessons.title: Reach Rouh from your phone
lessons.outcome: After this you can open Rouh in your phone's browser, wherever you are.

cover.alt: The Your Rouh page in Anatomy, with Rouh's address and the button to connect to rouh.land.

summary: Your Rouh at an address of its own, so your phone reaches it as easily as your desk does.
how: Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Your Rouh.
Under Your Rouh's URL, press Get its URL, then Turn on URL.
Press Show sign-in code, open the address on your phone and sign in. Add it to your home screen if you like.
On the phone, the chat and the canvas take turns, and the orb in the bottom-left corner opens the menu, as on a desk.
says: How can I reach you from the browser on my phone?

connection.needs: A Rouh connected to rouh.land. If this Rouh has no relay, the page says so and there is no address to turn on.

lessons.title: Talk to Rouh on Telegram
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh can message you, and you can answer it, from Telegram.

cover.alt: The Telegram page under Connections, with the steps to make a bot and the box for its token.

summary: Reminders, questions and decisions reach your phone, and you can answer them with a tap.
how: In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot and answer its two questions. Copy the token it gives you.
Open your new bot and press Start.
In Rouh, open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Telegram.
Paste the token into Bot token and press Save.
says: Send me a Telegram message saying hello.
Remind me on Telegram at five to leave.

connection.needs: Telegram on your phone, and a bot token from @BotFather.

lessons.title: Bring in your iCloud contacts
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh knows the people you know: their numbers, addresses and companies.

cover.alt: The Apple Contacts page under Connections, with the steps for an app-specific password and the Connect button.

summary: Rouh can find anyone in your contacts, show their card and keep it up to date.
how: At account.apple.com, open Sign-In and Security, then App-Specific Passwords. Press +, name it Rouh and press Create. Copy the password.
In Rouh, open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Apple Contacts.
Fill in Apple ID and App-specific password.
Press Connect. Rouh reads your contacts and keeps them in step.
says: Who do I know in Berlin?
What is Lena's phone number?

connection.needs: An Apple ID with two-factor sign-in on, and an app-specific password.

stages.title: Everyday wins
stages.why: The small things Rouh takes off your hands every day.

lessons.title: Set a reminder
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh reminds you of anything, at the time you say.

cover.alt: Clockwork: everything Rouh will say or do at a time, by day and hour.

summary: Say what and when, in plain words, and Rouh says it to you at that time: in the chat, and on Telegram if you have it.
how: Say the reminder: what, and a day or a time.
Rouh puts it in Clockwork and says when it will remind you.
Open Clockwork (menu, Work, Clockwork) to see everything coming up, and change or remove any of it.
says: Remind me tomorrow at nine to call the dentist.
Remind me in twenty minutes to take the bread out.
What is coming up?
Move the dentist reminder to ten.

lessons.title: Have Rouh do something on repeat
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh does a piece of work for you every day or week, by itself.

cover.alt: Clockwork, listing work that repeats every day at its time.

summary: Not only reminders: Rouh can do the work itself on a schedule, such as reading your calendar every Monday and telling you the week.
how: Say what to do and how often: every day, every Monday, the first of the month.
Rouh keeps it in Clockwork, marked with how often it runs.
Pause or change it in Clockwork, or by asking.
says: Every Monday at eight, tell me what is on my calendar this week.
Every evening at six, tell me what is still open today.
Stop the Monday calendar summary.

lessons.title: Go through your inbox
lessons.outcome: After this you know what came in and what needs an answer, without opening your mail.

cover.alt: Approvals: the emails and messages waiting for your OK, with the latest case listed.

summary: Let Rouh read the pile and tell you what matters. This needs Google connected (stage 1).
how: Ask what came in and what needs an answer. Rouh sums it up and says who is waiting.
Ask about any one email in more detail, or to find an old one.
When Gmail tells Rouh about new mail as it arrives (a switch on Enabling Rouh), Rouh tells you about what matters without being asked.
says: What came into my inbox today that needs an answer?
Find the email with last month's invoice.
Who have I not answered this week?

lessons.title: Answer an email with Rouh
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh writes your replies, and you only read and agree.

cover.alt: Approvals, where an email Rouh stopped on waits for your OK.

summary: Say who to answer and what to say, in a sentence. Rouh writes the draft and shows it to you before anything is sent.
how: Ask for a reply: who to, and what to say.
Read the draft Rouh shows you. Change anything, in words.
Tell it to send. Emails Rouh stopped on for your OK wait in Approvals, under Now in the menu.
says: Draft a reply to Lena saying Thursday works for me.
Make it warmer.
Send it.

lessons.title: Plan your day with the calendar
lessons.outcome: After this you can check and change your calendar by asking.

cover.alt: The Morning brief page, where today's calendar is shown.

summary: Your calendar, by asking: what is on, when you are free, and putting things in.
how: Ask what is on a day, or when you are free.
Ask Rouh to put something on your calendar, with a day and a time.
Ask to move or cancel something by naming it.
says: What is on my calendar tomorrow?
When am I free for an hour on Thursday?
Put lunch with Sam on Thursday at one.
Move lunch with Sam to Friday.

lessons.title: Read your morning brief
lessons.outcome: After this your day starts on one page: weather, calendar, news and mail.

cover.alt: Morning brief settings, with its switch, the time it is made and its sections.

summary: Each morning the brief puts the day on one page: the weather, your calendar, a few world stories, unread mail and reminders.
how: Open it from the menu: Now, then Morning brief.
Choose when it is made and what is in it in Morning brief settings (menu, Anatomy, Behaviour).
It can be switched on and off on Enabling Rouh, too.
says: Open my morning brief.
Leave the world news out of my brief.

lessons.title: Find someone in your contacts
lessons.outcome: After this a person's card, with Call, Text and Directions, is one question away.

cover.alt: A drawing: a question about Lena in the chat, and her contact card on the canvas with Call, Text and Directions.

summary: Ask about anyone by name, or by where they are or what they do. This needs your iCloud contacts (stage 1).
how: Ask about a person.
Rouh answers in the chat and opens their card on the canvas, with Call, Text and Directions.
When someone new writes to you, Rouh offers to save them to your contacts.
says: What is Lena's office address?
Who do I know in Berlin?
Save Sam Rivera's new number.

lessons.title: Connect and control your lights
lessons.outcome: After this you can set the lights in any room by saying so.

cover.alt: The Philips Hue page under Connections, with the Hue app's settings and Connect.

summary: Every Philips Hue light in the house, room by room, on the Home page and by voice.
how: Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Philips Hue.
Press Connect and sign in to Hue.
If Rouh cannot reach the bridge, press the round button on top of the bridge, then press Try again within 30 seconds.
Open Home to see every room's lights, or just say what you want.
says: What lights do I have?
Dim the living room lights to thirty percent.
Turn off all the lights.

connection.needs: A Hue account and a Hue bridge. The first time, an administrator gives Rouh a Hue app from developers.meethue.com.

lessons.title: Connect and run your robot vacuum
lessons.outcome: After this you can start, pause and dock the vacuum by saying so.

cover.alt: The Dreame page under Connections, with the account form and Connect.

summary: Clean a room, send the robot home or check its battery, from the Home page or by voice.
how: Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Dreame.
Pick the app the robot is in, then fill in your email and password.
Press Connect. If Xiaomi asks for a code, type it and press Verify.
Open Home to see the robot, or just say what it should do.
says: Is the vacuum charged?
Clean the kitchen.
Send the robot back to its dock.

connection.needs: A Dreame robot, and a Dreamehome account with a password (an account made with Apple or Google sign-in has none), or a Xiaomi Mi Home account.

lessons.title: Look something up
lessons.outcome: After this you get a quick, sourced answer without leaving the chat.

cover.alt: A drawing: a question in the chat, and Rouh's short answer with two sources under it.

summary: For a quick fact, ask Rouh to look into it. It reads the web and answers in a few sentences, with the sources it used.
how: Say look into, and the question.
The answer appears in the chat, with its sources numbered under it.
For a proper comparison with a recommendation, say research instead: that comes back as a task (stage 3).
says: Look into what the weather will be like in Lisbon next weekend.
Look into the opening hours of the Lisbon Oceanarium.

lessons.title: Have Rouh use a website while you watch
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh does errands on websites, and you step in when it needs you.

cover.alt: The Live browser page, where Rouh's browser is shown while it works.

summary: For errands on websites, Rouh uses a real browser that you can watch and take over.
how: Say what to do and on which site.
Watch it work in the Live browser (menu, Now, Live browser).
When it needs you, for a login, a code or a payment, press Take control, do that part, then press Hand back.
Rouh never types your passwords and never presses the final Book or Pay for you.
says: Find a table for two on Friday evening on a restaurant's own website, and stop before booking.

stages.title: Work with tasks
stages.why: Give your work a home, and Rouh keeps track of every piece of it.

lessons.title: Make a task
lessons.outcome: After this your work has a home, a number and a conversation of its own.

cover.alt: The task browser: every project and task, filed under Work, each with its number.

summary: A task is a home for one piece of work: its steps, its pages and its own conversation.
how: Ask Rouh to make a task, and to break it into steps if you like.
It appears in the task browser (menu, Work, Task browser), filed under Work or Personal, with a number.
Open it to see its steps, and talk about it in its own conversation.
says: Make a task for organising a team offsite in March, and break it into steps.
Open the offsite task.

lessons.title: Add a step and use its number
lessons.outcome: After this you can point Rouh at any piece of work by its number.

cover.alt: A task's page: its title, its number and its first step.

summary: Every task has a number, like 58, and its steps are 58-01, 58-02. Say the number and Rouh knows exactly what you mean.
how: Ask Rouh to add a step to a task.
Say a number to point Rouh at that work: what is happening with it, what is next, move it.
A new round of work on a task becomes its next numbered step.
says: Add a step to the offsite task: find three venues and compare them.
What is happening with 58-02?

lessons.title: Pin what you are working on
lessons.outcome: After this the Control room shows where you left off and what is next.

cover.alt: The Control room: what you pinned, where you left off and what is next.

summary: Pin the few tasks you are on this week. The Control room then shows each one, where you left off and what is next.
how: Say which task to pin, by name or number.
Open the Control room (menu, Work) to see your pinned work.
Unpin a task when it is done.
says: Pin the offsite task.
Pin 58 and unpin 19.

lessons.title: Ask for research
lessons.outcome: After this you get research back as a task, with its sources and a recommendation.

cover.alt: A task's page, where research comes back as a step with its findings.

summary: Ask Rouh to look into something properly, and the answer comes back as a task you can keep.
how: Say research or compare, and what.
Rouh hands the work to an assistant in the background, so you can carry on.
The result comes back as a task: the findings, their sources and Rouh's recommendation.
Ask for another round in the same task, and it becomes the next step.
says: Research which robot vacuum I should buy for a small flat with a cat.
Compare three project management apps for a team of five.

lessons.title: Share or publish a task
lessons.outcome: After this you can show your work to anyone, by email or by link.

cover.alt: A task's page, which can be shared with one person or published with a link.

summary: Sharing gives one email address access to a task, to view or to edit. Publishing makes its pages readable by anyone with the link.
how: To share with one person, give Rouh their email address and say view or edit.
They get an email with the link, and sign in to open it.
To publish, ask Rouh to publish the task.
Ask whether a task is public at any time.
says: Share the offsite task with sam@example.com so they can view it.
Publish 58.
Is 58 public?

stages.title: Let Rouh work for you
stages.why: Hand over whole pieces of work, and answer only what really needs you.

lessons.title: Hand Rouh a real piece of work
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh works in the background while you carry on.

cover.alt: Metabolism: every piece of work Rouh runs in the background.

summary: For anything bigger than a quick answer, Rouh starts work in the background and reports back.
how: Describe the work as you would to a colleague: what, where it should end up, and by when.
Rouh starts a run and tells you. Carry on with anything else.
If the work needs your answer, it waits in Decisions.
When it finishes, Rouh tells you what it did and where to find it.
says: Write a one-page plan for the offsite and put it in its task.
Stop that run.

lessons.title: Check what is running
lessons.outcome: After this you always know what Rouh is busy with.

cover.alt: The orb open over the whole screen: with nothing running, one calm light.

summary: Two places say what Rouh is busy with: the orb, which draws each piece of work as a branch, and Metabolism, which lists every run.
how: Open the orb over the whole screen (see Read the orb): each branch is work going on.
Or open Metabolism (menu, Evolution) for the list of runs, newest first.
Or just ask.
says: What is running right now?
How far is the offsite plan?

lessons.title: Answer a decision
lessons.outcome: After this you clear what waits on you, usually with one press.

cover.alt: Decisions: everything waiting on your answer; here, nothing waits.

summary: Everything that waits on your answer is in one place, Decisions, with Rouh's recommendation ready.
how: Open Decisions (menu, Now). The number on Now says how many are waiting.
Each decision says what each answer means, and which one Rouh recommends.
Press an answer. You can undo it for a short while after.
You can also answer by voice or on Telegram.
says: What is waiting on me?
Answer decision 12 with the recommended option.

lessons.title: Do your part
lessons.outcome: After this you know the few hands-on things only you can do.

cover.alt: Your part: what only you can do to unblock work Rouh is doing.

summary: Some things only you can do with your own hands, such as signing a paper or calling a bank. They wait in Your part, next to Decisions.
how: Open Your part (menu, Now).
Each item says what to do and everything you need to do it.
Press Done when you have, or Not doing this; the work waiting on it carries on.
says: What do I need to do?

lessons.title: Set a goal
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh plans the steps to something you want, and says who does each.

cover.alt: New goal: the box for your goal, how it works, and examples.

summary: Say what you want to reach, and Rouh writes the plan and keeps it moving.
how: Tell Rouh your goal and when you want to reach it.
Answer the few questions it asks.
Rouh writes a plan of steps, saying who does each one: you, Rouh or someone else.
Open Goals (menu, Work) to follow the plan.
says: My goal is to run a half marathon by June.
How is my half marathon goal going?

lessons.title: Start a quest
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh carries a long-running question forward on its own.

cover.alt: Quests: the long-running work the heartbeat carries.

summary: A quest is a long-running question that Rouh keeps working on at each heartbeat, such as finding a better deal.
how: Say what the quest is, and any limits, such as a budget.
Open Quests (menu, Work) to see each one and how far it is.
Rouh tells you when one has an answer.
says: Start a quest to find a cheaper phone plan for me.
How is the phone plan quest going?

lessons.title: Meet the heartbeat
lessons.outcome: After this you know what Rouh does by itself, and how to pause it.

cover.alt: The Heartbeat page: today, beat by beat, what Rouh did by itself.

summary: Every half hour in working hours the heartbeat checks Rouh's duties without being asked. It does only safe things by itself; anything else comes to you as a decision.
how: Open Heartbeat (menu, Work) to see what it did today, beat by beat.
Pause it there with Pause, or change its rhythm under its Settings tab.
Its switch is also on Enabling Rouh.
says: Is the heartbeat on, and what did it do today?
Pause the heartbeat.

stages.title: Make it yours
stages.why: Teach Rouh how you like things, and keep the parts of your life apart.

lessons.title: Give Rouh a rule
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh always, or never, does something the way you said.

cover.alt: Rules: what Rouh keeps to, grouped, each with its switch.

summary: Say a rule as you would to a new colleague: always this, never that. Rouh keeps it on the Rules page.
how: Say the rule, starting with From now on, always or never.
Rouh shows it on the Rules page (menu, Memory, Rules), where you can change it or turn it off.
When you correct Rouh twice about the same thing, make it a rule.
says: From now on, always write to me in short sentences.
Never book anything before nine in the morning.

lessons.title: Teach Rouh one of your words
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh understands your nicknames and shorthand.

cover.alt: Vocabulary: your own words, and what you mean by them.

summary: Say once what a word of yours means, and Rouh understands it from then on, by voice too.
how: Tell Rouh what the word or nickname means.
It lands in Vocabulary (menu, Memory).
Change or remove it there.
says: Remember that Bo means my brother Bob.
What does Bo mean?

lessons.title: Keep a thought
lessons.outcome: After this your ideas are kept in your words, and Rouh fills them out.

cover.alt: Thoughts: your own thoughts, kept in your words.

summary: A sentence that starts with Thought: is kept in your own words, and Rouh researches it into a fuller version later.
how: Start a sentence with Thought: and say the idea.
Open Thoughts (menu, Memory) to read them, each beside Rouh's fuller version.
says: Thought: we should try a four-day week in the summer.
Thought: a monthly dinner with the old team.

lessons.title: Keep parts of your life apart
lessons.outcome: After this work and family stay apart, each labelled with its own silo.

cover.alt: Silos: Work and Personal, each with its colour and who can see it.

summary: A silo is one part of your life, such as Work or Personal. Everything Rouh keeps is labelled with its silo, so the two never mix.
how: Open Silos (menu, Anatomy, You).
See which silos you have and what each holds.
Ask Rouh which silo something is in, or to move it.
says: Explain how my silos keep things apart.
Which silo is the offsite task in?

lessons.title: Choose which AI answers
lessons.outcome: After this you know which model answers, and how to trade quality for cost.

cover.alt: Models: the mode, Best, Balanced or Saver, and the providers.

summary: Trade quality for cost with one setting or one sentence.
how: Open Models (menu, Anatomy, Behaviour).
Pick a mode: Best, Balanced or Saver.
Each tier, Cheaper and Smart, has a model; every use of an AI in Rouh is on one of them.
Or say what you want, and Rouh changes the setting for you.
says: Which model answers my chats, and which mode are you in?
Switch to Saver.

stages.title: Security
stages.why: What always needs your yes, what Rouh never obeys, and how to see and close what is open to others.

lessons.title: Choose what needs your yes
lessons.outcome: After this the tools you pick always ask you before they act.

cover.alt: Permission gates: each tool, and whether it asks you first.

summary: Anything that sends, shares, publishes, pays or deletes stops and asks you first: the question lands in Decisions, with Rouh's recommendation. Permission gates add any other tool you choose to that list.
how: Open Permission gates (menu, Anatomy, Behaviour).
Turn on the gate for each tool that should ask you first, every time. The tools where a mistake costs money or cannot be undone are listed first.
A gate is kept by Rouh's code, not by its rules, so no words can talk Rouh past it. A yes is for that one call only.
says: Which of your tools ask me first before they act?
Always ask me before you send an email.

lessons.title: Restricted or Unrestricted
lessons.outcome: After this you know how much Rouh may do without asking, and how to switch it back.

cover.alt: Permissions: the switch between Restricted and Unrestricted, and what still asks you in every mode.

summary: Restricted is the normal mode: background work that sends, pays, deletes or changes a server waits for your yes. Unrestricted lets your own chats and runs do those things at once, for as long as you choose.
how: Open Permissions (menu, Anatomy, Behaviour). It says which mode you are in.
Only you can switch it, with a press on that page. Rouh, a run or an email cannot switch it for you.
Choose how long Unrestricted lasts: some hours, until you switch it back, or for good. When the hours are up, Restricted is back by itself.
Even in Unrestricted three things still ask you: money above your card's caps, deleting your data for good, and giving a password or account access to someone outside.
Work for a trusted contact, the heartbeat and anything about someone's email never get Unrestricted.
Everything that ran without asking is listed on the same page, under What Rouh did, with Undo where the service allows it.
says: Which mode are you in, Restricted or Unrestricted?
What would you still ask me about in Unrestricted?

lessons.title: Know what Rouh never obeys
lessons.outcome: After this you know why an email or a web page cannot give Rouh orders.

cover.alt: An email that tells Rouh to forward invoices to a stranger, and Rouh saying it will not, and what the email tried.

summary: Emails, web pages, documents and even file names are written by other people. Rouh reads them as information, never as instructions: only what you say to Rouh is an order.
how: Everything Rouh reads from outside arrives marked with where it came from, such as an email and its sender, so it is never mistaken for you.
If a message or a page tries to tell Rouh to do something, Rouh does not do it, and says so in one sentence: what it tried, and where.
Nothing is bought, sent or shared because a page, an email or a file said to. Only the work you asked for counts.
This is a rule on the Rules page, Text that is not from the person, and it is in every chat that reads mail or the web.
says: Read my newest email and tell me if it asks you to do anything.
Summarise this page, and say if it tries to give you orders.

lessons.title: Keep a secret in a box
lessons.outcome: After this you can hand Rouh a password that the AI never sees.

cover.alt: Boxes: a new box, with a name and the secret to keep.

summary: Never type a password into the chat. A box holds something the AI never sees: what you type goes straight into the database, sealed.
how: Ask Rouh for a box. A numbered box opens for you to type into.
Type the secret and press Save in the box. It goes straight into the database, sealed, and never through the chat.
To let Rouh use one, say open box and its number, in this chat. Only your own words open a box: never an email, a page or a job's report.
Open Boxes (menu, Memory) to see them all.
says: Give me a box for my Wi-Fi password.
Open box 3.

lessons.title: Add a trusted contact
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh can help someone you trust when they write to it.

cover.alt: Trusted contacts: the people Rouh may act for and answer, and what each may ask.

summary: Rouh can answer people you trust, and let one of them decide for you on a goal or task. Some things are never theirs: spending your money, deleting, publishing, sending or signing in your name, and changing Rouh.
how: Open Trusted contacts (menu, Memory).
Add a person and say what they may ask Rouh for.
When they write, Rouh helps them within what you allowed, and asks you about the rest.
To let someone decide for you on one goal or task, say so; their answers count there and nowhere else.
To take it back, set them to None in that task's Share panel, or tell Rouh. The very next thing they ask is refused.
says: Who are my trusted contacts, and what may each of them ask?
Let Sam decide for the offsite task.
Take Sam off the offsite task.

lessons.title: See what you have shared, and take it back
lessons.outcome: After this you can check who sees a task, and close it in one sentence.

cover.alt: A question, who can see task 58, and Rouh's answer: one person who can read, one who can edit, and a public link.

summary: Shared means one email address can read a task, or edit it if you said so. Published means anyone with the link can read it. Ask any time what is open, and close it with a sentence.
how: Ask Rouh who can see a task. It lists each person and what they may do, and whether the task is published.
Read lets them look. Edit lets them change its pages. A public link is always read only.
To take someone off, set them to None in the task's Share panel, or tell Rouh. Their link stops at once.
Where the Share panel shows Until, give a share an end: it is taken away by itself on that day.
To take a published task down, ask Rouh to unpublish it.
says: Who can see 58, and is it public?
Take sam@example.com off 58.
Unpublish 58.

lessons.title: Find the Drive files open beyond your company
lessons.outcome: After this you know which of your Drive files outsiders can open, and how to close them.

cover.alt: Rouh's answer listing Drive files: two anyone with the link can open, and three shared with people outside the company.

summary: Over months files get shared with clients and opened by link, and nobody closes them. Rouh reads your own Drive in one go and lists what is open beyond your company, widest first.
how: Connect Google first (the lesson Connect Google shows how).
Ask Rouh which of your files are open. It lists the files anyone with the link can open, then those shared with people or companies outside, each with what they may do.
Name one company or address to see only what they have.
To close a link, or take a person or a whole company off one file or all of them, say so. Drive does not email them when access is taken away.
To share a file for a while, say until when. Google ends the access by itself on that day.
If Rouh says one of these is switched off, turn it on in Evolution, Mutations.
says: Which of my Drive files are open beyond the company?
What have we shared with northwind.test?
Take dana@northwind.test off all my files.

lessons.title: Check your connections, and disconnect one
lessons.outcome: After this you know what Rouh can reach, and how to cut one off.

cover.alt: A connection's own page: what it reaches, its state, and the button that connects or disconnects it.

summary: Each connection opens one door for Rouh: Google your mail, calendar and Drive; Slack your team; Hue your lights. Close a door, and Rouh forgets the sign-in behind it.
how: Ask Rouh which connections are live. It says, for each, connected, needs attention, or not connected.
Open Connections (menu, Anatomy, Connections). Each connection has its own page, which says what it reaches.
On that page, press Disconnect. Rouh forgets its sign-in and keys, and stops using it at once.
The keys and tokens you give a connection are kept sealed in the database, and never put into the chat.
says: Which connections do you have, and are they all working?
What can you reach through my Google account?

stages.title: Power user
stages.why: The deep end: Rouh's memory, your team's tools, and changing Rouh itself. Every connection here is optional.

lessons.title: Look inside Rouh's memory
lessons.outcome: After this you can see what Rouh knows, and where it learned it.

cover.alt: Synapse: Rouh's memory, its datasets and how it is kept.

summary: Synapse is Rouh's memory: what it knows about people, places and your work, each fact with where it came from.
how: Open Synapse (menu, Anatomy, under Behaviour).
Open a dataset to see what is in it.
Ask what Rouh knows about someone, and where it learned it.
says: What do you know about my accountant?
Where did you learn that?

lessons.title: Connect your meeting library
lessons.outcome: After this any recorded meeting is a question away.

cover.alt: Keys under Connections, where the meeting library is set up.

summary: Every recorded meeting's notes, searchable by what was said and who said it.
how: Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Keys, and find Meeting library.
Press Set up, fill in Address and Key.
Press Save. Rouh checks the key with the library before it keeps it.
Ask about any meeting.
says: Find the meeting where we talked about pricing.
What did we agree in the last meeting about the budget?

connection.needs: Your meeting library's address and a key that starts with ml_.

lessons.title: Connect Slack and use it
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh can read, search and write in your Slack channels.

cover.alt: The Slack page under Connections: create Rouh's app, then paste its tokens.

summary: Your team's conversations, searchable and answerable from Rouh.
how: Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Slack, and press Create the app in Slack. In Slack press Next, then Create.
In Install App press Install to Workspace, then Allow.
In Basic Information, App-Level Tokens, press Generate Token and Scopes and add connections:write.
Paste the bot token, your user token and the app-level token into Rouh and press Save.
In each channel Rouh should see, type /invite @Rouh.
To tell Rouh who someone on Slack is, ask it to link them to their contact.
says: Which Slack channels can you see?
What did the team say about the launch today?
Link Sam on Slack to Sam's contact.

connection.needs: Permission to install apps in your Slack workspace.

lessons.title: Set up payments and Stripe
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh can pay within limits you set, and take payments through Stripe.

cover.alt: Payments under Money: the card vault and the Stripe key.

summary: A card kept sealed, with spending caps you choose, and Stripe for payment links.
how: Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Money, then Payments.
Press Add card, fill in the card and press Save card. Press Set caps to choose the limits.
For Stripe, paste a restricted key (Stripe: Developers, API keys, Create restricted key), press Save key, then Make the webhook.
Ask Rouh for a payment link when someone should pay you.
says: What cards are in my vault?
Make a payment link for 40 euros for the workshop.

connection.needs: Your card, and for Stripe a restricted key.

lessons.title: Add an MCP server and use its tools
lessons.outcome: After this another service's tools work from your conversation.

cover.alt: MCP servers under Connections, with Connect a server and the ready-made ones.

summary: An MCP server (a standard way for a service to offer its tools to an AI) gives Rouh that service's tools.
how: Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then MCP servers, and press Connect a server.
Pick one of the ready-made servers, or Your own, and fill in its name and address.
Press Test, and once it passes, press Save.
Ask Rouh to use it, by the service's name.
says: Which MCP servers are connected?
What can you do with the MCP servers I have connected?

connection.needs: The server's address and its token. A server that runs as a command needs an administrator.

lessons.title: Connect a domain on Cloudflare
lessons.outcome: After this your domain's records change when you say so.

cover.alt: The Cloudflare page under Connections, with Add a zone.

summary: Your domain's records, changed by asking, with nothing to click through.
how: Make a Cloudflare token for one zone: My Profile, API Tokens, Create Token, Custom token.
Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Cloudflare.
Under Add a zone, type the domain name and press Add zone.
Paste the token into its box and press Save. Rouh checks it.
says: Which records does my domain have on Cloudflare?
Point shop at the new server.

connection.needs: A Cloudflare token for one zone.

lessons.title: Ask Rouh to change itself
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh grows a new ability because you asked for it.

cover.alt: Gene therapy open beside the chat: How would you like to mutate me?, with a box and Mutate.

summary: Say what you would like Rouh to do differently. Rouh builds the change as a gene (one ability of Rouh), checks it, and puts it live.
how: Say improve yourself so, and what you want.
Or open Gene therapy (the menu's foot, beside Rouh), write it in the box and press Mutate.
Rouh tells you when the new gene is live.
says: Improve yourself so the morning brief also lists my birthdays this week.

lessons.title: See how Rouh evolves
lessons.outcome: After this you can keep or reject the new abilities Rouh tries out.

cover.alt: Mutations: every gene the nightly run built for you, waiting to be looked at.

summary: Every night Rouh may try out new genes for you. Mutations lists them, and you keep or reject each one.
how: Open Mutations (menu, Evolution).
Read what each new gene does.
Keep it, or reject it.
says: Which new genes are on trial for me?

lessons.title: Add an idea to the incubator
lessons.outcome: After this your idea waits, scored, until it is built.

cover.alt: The Incubator: ideas for genes, scored, until one hatches.

summary: Ideas for new genes wait in the Incubator, scored, until one is built.
how: Say the idea, and that it is for the incubator.
Open the Incubator (menu, Evolution) to see every idea and its score.
says: Add an idea to the incubator: a weekly summary of what I spent.

features.name: The heartbeat
features.what: Rouh's own turn, every half hour in working hours: it checks its duties, carries your quests forward and starts work nobody had to ask for. It only does safe things by itself; anything else comes to you as a decision.
features.off: Off, nothing beats by itself and quests wait; a yes you give in Decisions still runs.

features.name: The morning brief
features.what: One page every morning: the weather, your calendar, a few world stories, AI news from your YouTube channels, unread mail and reminders.
features.off: Off, no brief is made in the morning; you can still ask for one.

features.name: New mail as it arrives
features.what: Gmail tells Rouh the moment a new email lands, so Rouh can sort it and tell you about what matters, instead of waiting for you to ask.
features.off: Off, Rouh reads your mail only when you ask about it.

features.title: Features you can switch on and off
features.lede: The same switches as on their Settings pages: flip one here and it is flipped there.

tips.title: Numbers are addresses
tips.body: Every task and step has a number. Say it, and Rouh goes straight there: 58 is a task, 58-02 its second step.
says: What is happening with 58-02?

tips.title: Ask for several things in one breath
tips.body: You do not have to wait between requests. Say them together and Rouh does each one.
says: Remind me on Friday at nine to call Sam, and put lunch with Lena on Thursday at one.

tips.title: Take a run over, then hand it back
tips.body: A run of the one program can be yours for a while: say let me drive to take its terminal, and carry on to give it back.
says: Let me drive that run.

tips.title: Change course while it works
tips.body: You can talk to work that is already running, to steer it or answer what it is stuck on.
says: Tell that run to use the shorter opening.

tips.title: Secrets go in a box
tips.body: Never type a password into the chat. Ask for a box: what you put in it goes straight into the database and never reaches the AI.
says: Give me a box for my Wi-Fi password.

tips.title: Teach it your nicknames
tips.body: Say once what a word of yours means, and Rouh understands it from then on, by voice too.
says: Remember that Bo means my brother Bob.

tips.title: Start with Thought:
tips.body: A sentence that starts with Thought: is kept in your own words, and Rouh fills it out later.
says: Thought: a monthly dinner with the old team.

tips.title: Say it once, as a rule
tips.body: When you correct Rouh twice about the same thing, make it a rule. Say always or never and it sticks.
says: From now on, never book anything before nine in the morning.

tips.title: Pin this week's work
tips.body: Pin the few tasks you are on. The Control room then shows each one, where you left off and what is next.
says: Pin 58 and unpin 19.

tips.title: Change a card, do not ask for a new one
tips.body: Ask for a change to the card on the screen and Rouh revises it in place. Every version is kept, so you can go back.
says: What did that table say before you changed it?

tips.title: Keep a card with its work
tips.body: A card worth keeping can become a step of a task, so it is found with everything else about it.
says: File that card as a step of the offsite task.

tips.title: Let someone decide for you
tips.body: For one goal or task, a person you trust can answer in your place. Their answers count there and nowhere else.
says: Let Sam decide for the offsite task.

tips.title: One question clears the queue
tips.body: Ask what is waiting on you, and answer each by its number, in the same sentence if you like.
says: What is waiting on me?

tips.title: Read the orb's colours
tips.body: A branch marked NEEDS YOU is waiting on you. The rings round the orb are the machine: storage, then CPU, then memory, each green or grey while there is room, amber when busy, red when too busy.
says: What are you working on right now?

tips.title: Escape stops the answer, not the work
tips.body: Press Escape to stop Rouh mid-answer. Anything it already started in the background carries on.
says: What is running right now?

tips.title: Trade quality for cost in a sentence
tips.body: Pick Best, Balanced or Saver by asking, without opening Settings.
says: Switch to Saver.

tips.title: Research comes back as a task
tips.body: Say research or compare and you get a task with sources and a recommendation, not a quick answer. For a quick answer, say look into.
says: Look into what time the Lisbon Oceanarium opens on Sunday.

tips.title: Ask Rouh to change itself
tips.body: If Rouh cannot do something you want, say improve yourself so, and it grows the ability as a gene.
says: Improve yourself so the morning brief also lists my birthdays this week.

tips.title: Ask what is open, once a month
tips.body: Shares outlive the meeting they were for. Once a month ask what of yours is open to people outside: tasks you published or shared, and Drive files open with a link.
says: What of mine is open to people outside the company?
